content.user_title: Estimate Your Furusato Nozei Donation Limit
content.value_statement: Furusato nozei donation limits depend on income, household details, and tax deductions. This skill estimates your limit with published formulas, explicit assumptions, and intermediate calculations.
actual_capabilities: Estimate a donation limit using resident tax income levy and the applicable income tax rate.
Estimate taxable income from gross salary, salary deductions, household details, and assumed social insurance payments.
Distinguish income tax basic deductions from the resident tax basic deduction.
Show calculation assumptions, formulas, intermediate values, and approximate donation limits.
Explain the five-municipality one-stop condition and the effect of filing a tax return.
Refer complex deduction or income cases to an official simulator or tax professional.
limitations: Results are estimates, not guaranteed donation limits or individual tax advice.
The skill does not prepare tax returns or resolve complex income and deduction cases.
Tax tables reflect the author's September 2026 snapshot; verify the applicable tax year and current official rules.
The shared response checklist linked in the skill is not included in the reviewed package.

use_cases.title: Plan a Salary-Based Donation
use_cases.description: Estimate a donation budget from gross salary and household details, with clear assumptions and warnings.
use_cases.target_user: Salaried employees planning hometown tax donations

use_cases.title: Compare Household Assumptions
use_cases.description: Compare donation estimates when spouse or dependent deductions change, using the same salary and tax year.

use_cases.title: Explain Donation Procedures
use_cases.description: Explain basic one-stop conditions and identify when an official simulator or professional review is needed.

prompt_templates.title: Understand the Donation Limit
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the furusato nozei donation limit and the JPY 2,000 personal contribution. What information do you need to estimate mine?
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: understand the concept and required inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Estimate from Gross Salary
prompt_templates.prompt: For tax year [year], my gross salary is JPY [amount], with [spouse and dependent details]. Estimate my donation limit and list assumptions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: estimate from salary and household details.

prompt_templates.title: Calculate from Known Tax Figures
prompt_templates.prompt: My resident tax income levy is JPY [amount], and my income tax rate is [rate]%. Show the donation-limit formula and intermediate values.
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced: calculate with known tax figures.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Household Scenario
prompt_templates.prompt: For [year], compare [household scenarios] at salary JPY [amount]. Separate both tax bases, state assumptions, and identify cases requiring professional review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare assumptions without treating estimates as definitive advice.

output_examples.input: My resident tax income levy is JPY 303,000 and my income tax rate is 10%. Estimate my donation limit.
output: Resident tax special deduction ceiling: JPY 303,000 multiplied by 20% equals JPY 60,600.
Formula denominator: 90% minus 10% multiplied by 1.021 equals 79.79%.
Estimated donation limit: JPY 60,600 divided by 0.7979, plus JPY 2,000, gives approximately JPY 77,950.
This is an estimate based on your supplied figures, not a guaranteed limit.

output_examples.input: I earn JPY 6,000,000 and have mortgage and medical deductions. Can you give me an exact limit?
output: An exact limit cannot be established with this simplified calculation.
Mortgage and medical deductions can change the result.
Use a detailed official simulator or consult a tax office or tax professional.

output_examples.input: I donated to four municipalities and will file a tax return. Can I use the one-stop exception?
output: Filing a tax return invalidates the one-stop exception.
Include your donations through the donation deduction procedure in your tax return.
This skill explains the procedure but does not prepare your return.

best_practices: Provide the tax year, gross salary, household details, and known tax figures before requesting an estimate.
Review every assumption and keep income tax deductions separate from resident tax deductions.
Verify current official rules and seek professional guidance when deductions or income are complex.
anti_patterns: Treating an estimated limit as a guaranteed amount with only JPY 2,000 personal cost.
Applying income tax basic deductions directly to resident tax calculations.
Using the quick reference table without checking household details, deductions, or the applicable tax year.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide gross salary, spouse and dependent details, and the tax year. Include taxable income or resident tax income levy if known.

faq.question: Does this skill require an external API?
faq.answer: No. It provides arithmetic instructions and official reference links, without requiring an external API.

faq.question: Is the estimated limit guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. Deductions, income details, and assumptions can change the limit. Donations above the actual limit increase your personal cost.

faq.question: Does it prepare tax returns?
faq.answer: No. Tax return preparation and individual tax judgments are outside its scope.

faq.question: What does it explain about the one-stop exception?
faq.answer: It describes the five-municipality condition for salaried donors and notes that filing a tax return invalidates the exception.

faq.question: How current are the tax tables?
faq.answer: The author dates the tables to September 2026. Check current official rules and use deductions for the applicable tax year.
